sources.query: The Elements was written by Euclid

Euclid is the author of the Elements..why: The same statement as the Elements' byline, in many phrasings. It is stated as a title-and-author pair ('Elements by Euclid', 'the Elements of Euclid', about 1,700 mentions together) and as a sentence ('Euclid wrote the Elements', 'Euclid wrote his Elements', 'Euclid wrote Elements', 'Euclid wrote The Elements', about 250 mentions together; no single sentence form passes 100 on its own except the title-and-author pairs). Wikipedia's first sentence on the Elements states it whole. It is the inverse reading (author_of) of the edited fact.

notes: ABox contraction paired with mathematics-replace-0001: removes the revision's original fact (the Elements written by Euclid; written_by is functional). Mathematics has no worlds. Related is 'Is Euclid the author of the Elements?' (the inverse author_of), which is close to the direct question as a yes/no. Derived: the cardinality question asks about Apollonius of Perga (no before, since a work has one author; nobody writes the denial, 'Apollonius wrote the Elements' has 0 hits), and two compositions reach Euclid through 'the author of the Elements' and facts stated about him by name (his career in Alexandria, the Optics). The Euclidean algorithm was not used because Book VII of the Elements contains it, and Pythagoras was not used because his dates already rule him out. Evidence about the original fact comes from the revision. Unrelated near shares the kind of question; contraction is exempt from Rule 7.
